title: Retail Sales Performance Report (2023‑2024)
executive_summary: The cleaned retail order data shows solid growth in 2024, with total revenue increasing 10.1% year‑over‑year to $233,348.80. Revenue is led by the East region, while quarterly performance peaked in Q3. High‑discount Electronics orders, though few, contribute over 11% of revenue. Order values are highly variable, and a small number of customers drive a notable share of sales.

key_findings.statement: In 2023‑2024 the company generated $445,325.09 in revenue across 520 orders, yielding an average order value of $856.39.
Revenue by region shows East leading with $130,516.69, followed by North $124,845.75, West $99,428.16, and South $90,534.49.
Quarterly revenue in 2024 grew from $36,108.31 in Q1 to $71,674.99 in Q3, with Q4 at $68,948.71.
Total revenue rose from $211,976.29 in 2023 to $233,348.80 in 2024, a 10.08% increase.
There were 22 high‑discount (≥20%) Electronics orders contributing $50,035.33, representing 11.23% of overall revenue.
Order revenue averages $856.39 (median $313.28) with a standard deviation of $1,295.74, ranging from $5.27 to $7,844.02.
The dataset contains 222 distinct customers; the top customer generated $27,793.13, accounting for 6.24% of total revenue.

limitations: The analysis is limited to the cleaned order export; returns, cancellations, or post‑sale adjustments are not reflected.
Discount percentages are taken as recorded; any promotional nuances (e.g., bundled offers) are not captured.
Only two years of data are available, which may not represent longer‑term trends or seasonality beyond 2024.
conclusion: Retail sales are growing, driven by strong performance in the East region and a notable contribution from high‑discount Electronics orders. While average order value is healthy, revenue distribution is highly skewed, with the top customer accounting for over 6% of sales. Stakeholders should consider targeted regional strategies, monitor discount impacts, and explore ways to broaden the customer base to reduce concentration risk.
